FLASHCARD SET · AGES 4–5

Time & Daily Routine flashcards — the parent shelf: 41 cards to download and print.

The whole time deck for printing at home: forty-one time-and-routine cards for ages four to five, each with its parent tip, its three pills — age, subject, level — its download button and one-tap printing; the library is the parents’ side of the class, so everything happens on this one shelf.

This is the parents’ copy of Class 41 · Time & Daily Routine: all forty-one time-and-routine cards on one shelf, ready to print. You do not need a plan — pick the time word your day needs most, download the card, and print it full size on A4 or Letter paper. Every card carries its parent tip underneath and four pills on top: the age it suits, the shelf it belongs to, the grade level to start at, and the skill it builds. The download button takes the full-size card; the print button runs a single card through your printer with nothing else on the page. There are no card pages to hop through: the shelf is the whole set.

The shelf is yours; the lesson is your child’s. The class page at Time & Daily Routine teaches each rule the way a teacher would — spoken to your child, the rule quoted word for word, one thing to try today — while this wall simply holds the deck for printing. Same forty-one cards, two jobs: the lesson lives in the class, the library is where parents print.

THE THREE LEVELS

Preschool, Grade 1, Grade 2.

Every card wears a level pill so tonight’s card takes one glance to choose. The levels are a suggested order, not a test — the time word your day needs most is always the right card.

  1. 01

    Preschool · Name it

    the eleven time names to point at first — the seven days, the twelve months, the parts of the day and the clock’s short hand.

  2. 02

    Grade 1 · Do it

    the eighteen routines and order words — the day’s steps, the chores, the plan, and the first-next-last family that holds them.

  3. 03

    Grade 2 · Own it

    the twelve bigger ideas — comparing how long things take, counting the waits, reading the whole time-word family and going with a changed plan.
